key_insight: Autoregressive video generators struggle to preserve important details over long rollouts because their usable memory is limited. This paper focuses on how to carry forward the most useful past information so future frames stay consistent and coherent.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in long-horizon autoregressive video generation: as sequences grow, models cannot keep all past context due to fixed context windows, storage limits, and compute constraints, which leads to losing identities, objects, and scene continuity.
method: Introduces a memory mechanism for autoregressive video generation that selectively preserves and reuses important historical information.
Targets the retention of critical long-term details such as entity identities, scene structure, and temporal consistency under bounded context constraints.
Designs the generation process to make better use of past frames without requiring unbounded attention or full-sequence storage.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the practicality of long video generation by making outputs more stable and temporally consistent. It is especially relevant for world models, interactive agents, and any application that needs extended visual continuity.

paper_title: The Past Frames the Future: Memory for Autoregressive Video Generation
paper_authors: Harold Haodong Chen, Rongjin Guo, Disen Lan, Wen-Jie Shu, Hongfei Zhang
